_note: Disease presets; cfg['disease'] = selected preset (config.load_config). Durations in days as gamma {mean, sd}, converted to steps with run.step_min (min 1 step). latent_days = infection -> start of infectiousness (E); presym_days = infectious before onset (I_pre); infectious_days = POST-onset infectious period (I_sym/I_asym), so total infectious = presym + infectious_days. Viral-load curve (peak 1.0 at onset): I_pre ramps exponentially from presym_start_level to 1.0; afterwards decays exponentially to end_level at t_end; x asym_rel_infectiousness if asymptomatic; x individual multiplier ~ Gamma(shape k, mean 1) clipped at individual_infectiousness_max (k<1 = superspreading). Close-contact hazard per susceptible per step = transmission_scale * close_hazard_per_min[tier] * step_min * infectiousness_src * (1-source_eff if src masked) * (1-wearer_eff if sus masked) * (outdoor_multiplier if not indoor); only same-room / both-outdoor pairs (wall=False), tiers 1-3. Aerosol: well-mixed box per indoor room, emission = quanta_per_hour_peak * infectiousness * emission_multiplier_by_activity[source activity] * (1-source_eff); loss rate = room ACH + decay_per_hour; dose = breathing_m3_per_h[susceptible activity] * step-mean concentration * dt_h * (1-wearer_eff); hazard = transmission_scale * dose. p_infect = 1-exp(-(H_close+H_aero)). Imports: per-step prob from archetype param import_daily_p * import_scale. Run disease.calibration_report(cfg) (scripts/smoke_disease.py) for analytic scenario probabilities.

influenza._note: Seasonal flu. Latent ~1.5 d, presym ~1 d, post-onset ~5 d (total infectious ~6 d), 30% asymptomatic at half infectiousness. Calibration targets (integrator tunes transmission_scale for campus R~1.3-2.0): dorm roommate SAR ~20-30%/episode (8 h sleep + 2 h relax/day co-located at 2-5 m in a 54 m^3, 2 ACH double), 1-h seminar with a peak-infectious person ~1% per susceptible (144 m^3, 4 ACH; 15%/40% of the hour within 1-2 m / 2-5 m), 3-h party near an infectious friend ~8% (300 m^3, 2 ACH, 25/50/25% at tiers 1/2/3). Pure Wells-Riley makes small bedrooms ~10x riskier per hour than seminars, so reconciling the roommate and seminar targets uses low emission while sleeping (emission x0.5, breathing 0.25 m^3/h) and moderate overdispersion (k=1). quanta_per_hour_peak=12 is at the low end of literature flu quanta (~15-100 q/h, Rudnick&Milton 2003 ~ 67 for an outbreak) because 'infectiousness' integrates to ~1.6 peak-days per symptomatic case and our rooms are well-mixed boxes. decay = 0.3/h deposition + ~0.3/h inactivation. Close tier weights 1 : 0.5 : 0.17 per min (3.6e-4, 1.8e-4, 6e-5).

severity._note: peak ~ Beta(a,b) (mean 0.57); severity = peak * shape: onset_fraction -> 1 over rise_days, then linear to end_fraction at t_end. 0 unless I_sym.

covid19._note: SARS-CoV-2 (Omicron-era-ish). Latent ~3 d, presym ~2 d (substantial presymptomatic spread: start level 0.25), post-onset ~6 d (total infectious ~8 d), 35% asymptomatic at 0.6 relative infectiousness, strong overdispersion (k=0.4). Aerosol emission ~2.5x flu (quanta 30 q/h peak); slightly higher close weights. Milder mean severity in young adults.

norovirus._note: Norovirus. Latent ~1.2 d, short presym ~0.3 d, post-onset ~2.7 d (total ~3 d), 30% asymptomatic at 0.3. Dominated by close contact (droplets from vomiting, shared surfaces approximated as proximity): close weights ~3x flu, outdoor multiplier higher (0.3); aerosol low (3 q/h, fast settling decay 1.5/h). Fomite / environmental route is NOT modeled. Masks less effective against this route. High severity.
